gaps.text: In-line measurement of Product temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: synchronised NIR reflection and Raman spectra merged into one augmented matrix, as in the published feed-frame example. Both probes must sample the same product volume at the same port, with data normalised to a common time step. Each method keeps its own calibration block, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs before the second instrument is kept.)
Achievable in-line accuracy for fat and protein in this specific concentrated product
Suitable installation point and probe design for the customer's line

items.finding: The study notes that the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, requiring tempered sample holders.
items.how_it_applies: This highlights that product temperature fluctuations could impact NIR measurements in aqueous dairy products, suggesting that testing temperature compensation or sample conditioning might be necessary.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source discusses biopharmaceutical downstream processing and general aqueous solutions rather than an in-line flowing opaque milk product, so thermal dynamics may differ.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E03 ¶12

items.finding: Continuous processes at a fixed probe location can operate in a steady-state window, simplifying model design by allowing narrower calibrations centered on the operational envelope.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests that if data fusion methods are implemented, establishing a steady-state operating window could simplify the calibration and validation of the combined models.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source refers to liquid-liquid extraction in lithium recycling rather than milk processing, and does not specifically address multi-method sensor fusion.

citation.quote: In contrast, a continuous process at a fixed probe location is intended to operate in a steady-state window, which simplifies the model design: calibrations can be narrower and centered on the operational envelope, validation can rely on independent steady-state runs, and online monitoring focuses on drift and out-of-specification detection rather than resolving the rapidly changing composition.
citation.label: E02 ¶8
